questions.problem:
The linear transformation $T$ and the vector $b\in {R}^{4}$ are given below. Determine if there exists a vector $x\in {R}^{4}$ such that $T(x)=b.$
In the affirmative case, find the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{4},$ where ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3},{x}_{4}$ are the components of $x.$  

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3} \\ {x}_{4}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}-2{x}_{4} \\ 3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}+4{x}_{4} \\ 7{x}_{4}-4{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3} \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 5 \\ -3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we write down the standard matrix of $T:$

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & -2 \\ 3 & 5 & -2 & 4 \\ -4 & -1 & -3 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Since $T$ is the standard matix of $T,$ we have $\text{Im}(T)=\text{Col}(T).$ In order to determine whether $b$ lies in $\text{Im}(T),$ we need to check if the equation $Tx=b$ is consistent. 

So, let's find the row echelon form of the augmented matrix $[T\,|\,b]$ as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}[T\,|\,b] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & -2 & 5 \\ 3 & 5 & -2 & 4 & 5 \\ -4 & -1 & -3 & 7 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+4{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & -2 & 5 \\ 0 & 2 & -2 & 10 & -10 \\ 0 & 3 & -3 & -1 & 17 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-\frac{3}{2}{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & -2 & 5 \\ 0 & 2 & -2 & 10 & -10 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -16 & 32 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has three pivot columns (the $1$st, $2$nd and the $4$th). Hence ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. 
Now, from the third equation we get 

$$
-16{x}_{4}=32\,⟹\,{x}_{4}=-2.
$$

Substituting this into the second equation gives

$$
2{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}+10(-2)=-10\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=5+{x}_{3}.
$$

Then, substituting ${x}_{2}=5+{x}_{3}$ and ${x}_{4}=2$ into the first equation we obtain 

$$
{x}_{1}+(5+{x}_{3})-2(-2)=5\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-4-{x}_{3}.
$$

As a result, the general solution is given by 

$$
[\begin{aligned}-4-{x}_{3} \\ 5+{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3} \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Setting ${x}_{3}=0$, we have

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 5 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]
$$

where $T(x)=b.$

Finally, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{4}=-4+5-2=-1.$

questions.problem:
The linear transformation $T$ and the vector $b\in {R}^{4}$ are given below. Determine if there exists a vector $x\in {R}^{4}$ such that $T(x)=b.$
In the affirmative case, find the value of $w+x-z,$ where $w,x,y,z$ are the components of $x.$  

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}w \\ x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}w+3z-x-2y \\ 4x-2w+y-6z \\ 3w+5x+10z-16y \\ 5y-w-3z-x\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -5 \\ 4 \\ 5\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we write down the standard matrix of $T:$

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -2 & 3 \\ -2 & 4 & 1 & -6 \\ 3 & 5 & -16 & 10 \\ -1 & -1 & 5 & -3\end{aligned}]
$$

Since $T$ is the standard matix of $T,$ we have $\text{Im}(T)=\text{Col}(T).$ In order to determine whether $b$ lies in $\text{Im}(T),$ we need to check if the equation $Tx=b$ is consistent. 

So, let's find the row echelon form of the augmented matrix $[T\,|\,b]$ as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}[T\,|\,b] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -2 & 3 & 4 \\ -2 & 4 & 1 & -6 & -5 \\ 3 & 5 & -16 & 10 & 4 \\ -1 & -1 & 5 & -3 & 5\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -2 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & 2 & -3 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 8 & -10 & 1 & -8 \\ 0 & -2 & 3 & 0 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-4{R}_{2} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -2 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & 2 & -3 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 1 & -20 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 12\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From the fourth equation, we get the false statement $0=12.$ Therefore, the system is inconsistent, and we conclude that  $b\notin \text{Im}(T).$

questions.problem:
The linear transformation $T$ and the vector $b\in {R}^{4}$ are given below. Determine if there exists a vector $x\in {R}^{4}$ such that $T(x)=b.$
In the affirmative case, find the value of $w-x+y,$ where $w,x,y,z$ are the components of $x.$  

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}w \\ x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}w-3x-2z \\ 2x-2w-4y \\ 3w-y-10x-7z \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we write down the standard matrix of $T:$

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 0 & -2 \\ -2 & 2 & -4 & 0 \\ 3 & -10 & -1 & -7 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Since $T$ is the standard matix of $T,$ we have $\text{Im}(T)=\text{Col}(T).$ In order to determine whether $b$ lies in $\text{Im}(T),$ we need to check if the equation $Tx=b$ is consistent. 

So, let's find the row echelon form of the augmented matrix $[T\,|\,b]$ as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}[T\,|\,b] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 0 & -2 & 3 \\ -2 & 2 & -4 & 0 & 2 \\ 3 & -10 & -1 & -7 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 0 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & -4 & -4 & -4 & 8 \\ 0 & -1 & -1 & -1 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-\frac{1}{4}){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 0 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & -4 & -4 & -4 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & -8 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get the false statement $0=-8.$ Therefore, the system is inconsistent, and we conclude that  $b\notin \text{Im}(T).$

questions.problem: If $T=[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 4 \\ 9 & -8 & 10 \\ -3 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}]$ is the standard matrix of the linear transformation $T$, then $\text{rank}(T)=$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that $\text{rank}(T)=\text{dim}(\text{Im}(T))=\text{rank}(T).$ 

So, we need to find the rank of the matrix $T.$ We reduce $T$ to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 4 \\ 9 & -8 & 10 \\ -3 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & -2 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, since $T$ has $3$ pivot column, we have that 

$$
\text{rank}(T)=\text{rank}(T)=3.
$$

questions.problem: Given the transformation $T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}2y+z \\ -y+5x \\ -5x+y\end{aligned}],$ find its rank.
questions.worked_solution:
First, the standard matrix of $T$ is given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & 1 \\ 5 & -1 & 0 \\ -5 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Recall that $\text{rank}(T)=\text{dim}(\text{Im}(T))=\text{rank}(T).$ 

So, we need to find the rank of the matrix $T.$ We reduce $T$ to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & 1 \\ 5 & -1 & 0 \\ -5 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}5 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 \\ -5 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}5 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, since $T$ has $2$ pivot columns, we have that 

$$
\text{rank}(T)=\text{rank}(T)=2.
$$
